title: Autonomous routing fallbacks & ops runbook
body:
TL;DR: This doc captures a pragmatic, operational-first approach for autonomous request steering across regions and control-plane failure modes. It combines architecture notes with inline runbook steps and a decision tree that on-call can follow without flipping between multiple pages. Use this during incidents, tabletop exercises, and when onboarding new SREs/Platform engineers.

Context / Why this exists:
- We operate multi-region clusters and a lightweight control plane that issues routing decisions (policies, capacity hints, fallbacks). Past incidents showed most outages were not full-region failures but degraded routing (stale capacity data, control-plane latencies, or misapplied policies).
- Goal: make routing degradation survivable with minimal manual intervention, keep SLOs for p99 latency and error-rate, and avoid cascading capacity churn during failovers.

High-level architecture (short):
- Data-plane: region-local inference fleets (hosted/dedicated/private variants). Each fleet exposes health + capacity metrics and accepts steering hints via the local router.
- Control-plane: policy service + global state writer (etcd-backed) that publishes region affinity, circuit-breaker state, and TTLed capacity snapshots.
- Edge/Ingress: stateless edge tier that consults the local routing cache first, then control-plane when cache misses.
- Fallback tiers: same-region degraded model pools, cross-region warm-failovers, last-resort queued requests for low-priority traffic.

Design principles (ops-forward):
1) Prefer conservative, reversible actions (toggle routing weights down vs. abrupt cutovers).
2) Rate-limit automated failovers (avoid flip-flopping).
3) Keep control-plane writes idempotent and observable (audit log per change).
4) Automated evacuation of non-critical traffic instead of wholesale region failover.

Key signals to watch (alerts):
- Control-plane API 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 2m.
- Control-plane median latency > 300ms for 3m.
- Global routing cache miss rate > 10% for 1m.
- Region X health score drop: p95 token throughput below baseline or host count < 80% of target.
- Traffic amplification (retries) causing >20% increase in server-side errors.

Incident decision tree (quick):
1) Is traffic loss or latency localized to single region? (yes/no)
  - Yes: follow "Region degraded" flow.
  - No: check control-plane health (go to step 2).
2) Is control-plane showing elevated errors/latency? (yes/no)
  - Yes: follow "Control-plane impairment" flow.
  - No: investigate edge/ingress or external network.

Region degraded (operational steps):
- Immediate (first 5m):
  1) Triage owner: on-call platform engineer acknowledges and posts to #platform-incident with short description and tag region.
  2) Check region fleet dashboards: host health, queue length, model load.
  3) If host_count < 75% -> check autoscaler logs (K8s/instance provisioning). If autoscaling failing, escalate to infra team and open JIRA (PLT-874).
  4) If host_count normal but p95 latency high -> check disk/memory pressure and model load; consider temporary model-scale-down for heavy models.
- Fallback (5–20m):
  Option A (conservative): reduce routing weight to region by 30% using the policy API (PATCH /v1/policies/steering) with dry-run flag. Wait 2m for metrics. If errors reduce, continue staged ramp down.
  Option B (aggressive): enable cross-region warm-failover for specific customer tiers only (target control-plane flag: allowXRegionWarmFailover=true). This preserves business-critical traffic.
- Recovery (20m+): once metrics stable at target, incrementally restore weights back in 10% steps every 5–10m. Document every policy change in incident timeline.

Control-plane impairment (operational steps):
- Short-circuit policy reads:
  1) If control-plane API latency is high, flip edge tier to local routing-cache-only mode (environment toggle: EDGE_ROUTING_MODE=CACHE_ONLY). This prevents cascading timeouts to control-plane.
  2) Notify control-plane on-call and publish heap/GC/latency traces.
  3) If API error rate > 5% for 5m, enable read-only degraded mode: lock policy writes and mark global state as "stale" (set controlplane.state=STALE with TTL). This will make the edge prefer cached policies and avoid churn.
- Short-term fallback: use last-known-good snapshots to keep routing decisions stable. If snapshots are missing, fall back to static regional weights defined in /ops/static-wts.json (checked into infra repo).
- If control-plane cannot be recovered within 30m: execute coordinated partial rollbacks (see Rollback checklist).

Misrouting / policy misapplication scenario:
- Detection: sudden spike in cross-region traffic where region affinity tags unchanged, or clients from EU routed to us-west consistently.
- Mitigation steps:
  1) Check policy audit log: who/what changed routing table recently (audit id + timestamp). Use: curl -sS $AUDIT_API/?since=2025-01-01 | jq . | grep <region>.
  2) If a bad policy update is found, revert to previous policy using the policy rollback endpoint (POST /v1/policies/{id}/rollback) and add "manual":true.
  3) If rollback fails, apply emergency override: set per-edge override file (/etc/edge/overrides/region-hints.json) with pinned region affinities; restart edge routing agent (systemctl restart edge-router).

Capacity pressure & traffic storms:
- Early signal: sustained 20% above expected QPS for 5m, autoscaler not bringing up capacity (or warm pools exhausted).
- Steps:
  1) Throttle non-critical routes using token bucket rules at the edge (edge-config throttle-rules).
  2) Enable request coalescing and prefix caching for repeated requests (toggle CACHE_PREFIXING=true).
  3) If still overloaded, use graceful degradation policies: downgrade model family (e.g., from redwood-xl to redwood-large) for low-priority customers via rollout: PATCH /v1/rollouts with selector=priority:low.

Rollback checklist (control-plane):
- Confirm current vs previous schema version (controlplane.schema_version).
- Ensure audit log captured and stored externally (S3).
- Notify downstream teams (console, hosting, SRE) before making changes.
- Execute rollback in small batches and monitor for immediate regressions.

Playbook primitives (ops commands):
- Check control-plane health: curl -sS https://controlplane.redwood.internal/health | jq .
- Get routing cache hit rates: curl -sS https://edge-metrics/metrics | grep routing_cache_hit
- Reduce region weight by 30% (example): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -X PATCH https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/policies/steer -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","delta_weight":-0.3,"reason":"ops emergency"}'
- Toggle cache-only mode on edge: kubectl -n edge set env deploy/edge-router EDGE_ROUTING_MODE=CACHE_ONLY

Escalation matrix / contacts (order):
1) Platform on-call: paging -> #platform-oncall, phone: +1-415-555-0112 (Pager Asha Patel)
2) Control-plane SME: Miguel Rivera (Slack @miguelr)
3) Infra/autoscaler: Evelyn Cho (Slack @evelync)
4) SRE lead for postmortem & follow-up: Samir Khan

Runbook testing & exercises:
- Quarterly tabletop: simulate a control-plane latency event with canary traffic and confirm edge cache-only mode transitions within 90s.
- Chaos: weekly chaos-probe that toggles region weight down to emulate partial capacity loss; verify rollback automation does not flip-flop for >10m.
- Measure: record time-to-safe-state (TTSS) for each exercise; goal TTSS < 8m for region degradation and < 3m for control-plane cache-only switch.

Open action items (TODOs):
- [ ] Add automated snapshot backups every 5m instead of 15m (Evelyn).
- [ ] Harden policy rollbacks to be multi-signed for prod (security review).
- [ ] Create a low-cost warm pool for EU region to reduce cold-start failovers (infra ticket).

Post-incident notes template (to copy into timeline):
- Incident start: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Signal that alerted: <alert name>
- Initial hypothesis: <short blurb>
- Mitigation steps taken (with timestamps)
- Rollbacks / policy changes (with audit ids)
- Recovery confirmation metrics
- Next steps / action owners

Appendix: quick references
- Policy API spec: https://confluence.redwood/policy-api
- Edge routing agent logs path: /var/log/edge-router/*.log
- Control-plane dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/d/controlplane

Notes to reader: This doc is intentionally operational and iterative. If you update the decision thresholds or commands, add a short changelog entry at the top of the file with date and initials. When in doubt during an incident, prefer short, observable changes over broad configuration churn.
